headline: 3 teens detained as phone recovered from suspect's house in Opratim's murder
summary: The 13-year-old son of a Comilla University teacher was found dead near the university campus after going missing for 24 hours.
details: 13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, a Class VII student at Comilla Border Guard Public School, was found dead near Comilla University on Saturday afternoon.
Opratim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor of Bangla at Comilla University, and businessman KM Firoz Shahriar.
The boy had left home on Friday afternoon, telling his parents he was going out to take photographs with his mother's iPhone.
Police have since recovered the missing iPhone from the house of a suspect named Tuhin, following leads from CCTV footage.
Three young men, identified as Tuhin, Anas, and Fahim, aged between 18 and 20, have been detained in connection with the alleged killing.
Inspector Mofiz Uddin Bhuiyan confirmed the recovery of the phone, while police are currently analyzing CCTV footage and questioning the suspects.
Cumilla Superintendent of Police Anisuzzaman is expected to brief the media on the investigation's progress.
caption:
A 13-year-old boy's body was found near Comilla University 24 hours after he went missing. Now, 3 teens are detained.

13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, a Class VII student at Comilla Border Guard Public School, was found dead near Comilla University on Saturday afternoon.

Opratim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor of Bangla at Comilla University, and businessman KM Firoz Shahriar.

The boy had left home on Friday afternoon, telling his parents he was going out to take photographs with his mother's iPhone.

Police have since recovered the missing iPhone from the house of a suspect named Tuhin, following leads from CCTV footage.

Three young men, identified as Tuhin, Anas, and Fahim, aged between 18 and 20, have been detained in connection with the alleged killing.

Inspector Mofiz Uddin Bhuiyan confirmed the recovery of the phone, while police are currently analyzing CCTV footage and questioning the suspects.

Cumilla Superintendent of Police Anisuzzaman is expected to brief the media on the investigation's progress.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman to [[make first UNGA address]] in New York
headline: PM Tarique Rahman to make first UNGA address in New York
summary: The Prime Minister will outline Bangladesh's new vision and democratic transition during the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is traveling to New York for the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), where he will deliver his first address to the forum on Thursday.
He becomes the third member of his family to address the assembly, following his father, late president Ziaur Rahman, and his mother, late prime minister Khaleda Zia.

The Prime Minister is scheduled to hold over a dozen high-level bilateral meetings with world leaders, including the Prime Ministers of Canada, Thailand, Bhutan, and Pakistan, as well as the UN Secretary-General.
During his visit, Tarique Rahman will also attend a dinner hosted by US President Donald Trump.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir stated that the address will focus on Bangladesh's new vision, democratic transition, and national aspirations.
The Rohingya crisis remains a top priority, with the government planning a high-level side event to discuss the complex situation.
Foreign Minister Dr. Khalilur Rahman is presiding over the 81st General Assembly as its President, marking the second time a Bangladeshi has held this position.
The visit is guided by a 'Bangladesh First' foreign policy, aiming to present the country as a democratic, confident, and responsible member of the international community.
caption:
PM Tarique Rahman heads to New York for his first-ever UNGA address, with a packed schedule of meetings with world leaders.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is traveling to New York for the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), where he will deliver his first address to the forum on Thursday.

He becomes the third member of his family to address the assembly, following his father, late president Ziaur Rahman, and his mother, late prime minister Khaleda Zia.

The Prime Minister is scheduled to hold over a dozen high-level bilateral meetings with world leaders, including the Prime Ministers of Canada, Thailand, Bhutan, and Pakistan, as well as the UN Secretary-General.

During his visit, Tarique Rahman will also attend a dinner hosted by US President Donald Trump.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir stated that the address will focus on Bangladesh's new vision, democratic transition, and national aspirations.

The Rohingya crisis remains a top priority, with the government planning a high-level side event to discuss the complex situation.

Foreign Minister Dr. Khalilur Rahman is presiding over the 81st General Assembly as its President, marking the second time a Bangladeshi has held this position.

The visit is guided by a 'Bangladesh First' foreign policy, aiming to present the country as a democratic, confident, and responsible member of the international community.
